newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong makes record seizure of pirated CDs.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong makes record seizure of pirated CDs.

text.p: Hong Kong customs officers have dented the activities of copyright pirates with a record seizure of counterfeit compact discs worth about HK$4.6 million (US$594,000), the Customs and Excise Department said on Friday.
Officers seized a record 116,000 pirated CDs and arrested two men after raiding a warehouse on Thursday, the department said.
Customs officers believe the pirated products were smuggled into Hong Kong for sale in the local market, it said.

"The crackdown on the syndicate is a reflection of the effort of Hong Kong customs in the fight against copyright piracy, which is not only directed at the retail level but also goes hard against syndicates masterminding the importation and distribution of pirated CDs," the department said.
Customs conducted more than 1,000 raids last year and seized about one million pirated CDs worth an estimated HK$47 million, it added.
Copyright piracy has become a sticking point in trade relations between Hong Kong and the United States.
A move by the U.S. Trade Representative's office to place the territory on the Special 301 watch list on intellectual property rights protection brought objections from the government on Thursday.

"Given the considerable and persistent anti-piracy efforts and initiatives the government has made, we consider it most unjustified to place Hong Kong on the 'Watch List'," a government spokesman said.
A persistently poor record could earn U.S. trade sanctions.
Hong Kong depends heavily on trade with the United States, which is its main trading partner after China.
